2026-11-23.title: Monday after the Sunday of the Annunciation · St Clement, Pope; St Felicity
readings: The hearts of the saints refreshed
A tree is known by its fruit
2026-11-23.alt: St Clement of Rome, Pope (late 1st century), author of a letter to the Church in Corinth (History); St Felicity, Roman martyr (Tradition). Anniversary of the erection of the Eparchy of St Ephrem of Khadki (2019).
2026-11-23.verse: The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, and the evil person out of evil treasure produces evil; for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.
theo: The short letter to Philemon begins with warmth. Paul, a prisoner, thanks God for Philemon's love and faith, and tells him: “the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, my brother.” Some Christians are like a cool drink on a hot day; their love refreshes everyone around them. Their goodness flows from a heart rooted in Christ.

Jesus says the same in a picture: a good tree does not bear bad fruit; each tree is known by its own fruit. Figs do not grow on thorns. And the fruit of the human tree is above all our words: “it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks.” To change our speech we must change our heart; to change our heart we must stay close to the one who is good. St Clement, who wrote to the quarrelling Corinthians, knew that peace in the Church begins in the heart.
outline: What do my words reveal about my heart?
“Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.”

2026-11-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, make my heart a good treasure, so that my words may bring life. Through the prayers of St Clement and St Felicity, let my love refresh the hearts of your saints. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the short letter to Philemon begins with warmth. Paul, a prisoner, thanks God for Philemon's love and faith: the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, my brother (Philemon 7). The very presence of some people is a comfort to others.

In the Gospel Jesus says: no good tree bears bad fruit; each tree is known by its own fruit. The good person out of the good treasure of the heart produces good, for it is out of the abundance of the heart that the mouth speaks (Luke 6:43–45).

Today the Church remembers Pope St Clement and St Felicity, trees that bore fruit. Our words reveal our heart. Today speak one word that refreshes someone's heart: a thank you, an encouragement, a blessing. Amen.
kids: Children, a good tree gives good fruit; a good heart speaks good words. Say three kind words to others today!

intro: Theme: “Out of the abundance of the heart.”

sub: The springs of life flow from the heart.

sub: A true friend loves at all times.

q: A friend loves at all times, and kinsfolk are born to share adversity.
I have indeed received much joy and encouragement from your love, because the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through you, my brother.

concl: A good heart bears good fruit.
